summary: Site for a video game (often from a small studio): key art and a click-to-load trailer, press quotes, game pillars, a facts ledger, screenshots, a dev diary and a launch email; a media page with every trailer and a screenshot mosaic; and a press kit with a fact sheet, copy-ready texts and downloads.

pages.purpose: Make a player want it in one screen (key art, title, trailer), say what kind of game it is, show it, and collect wishlists or launch emails.

sections.purpose: Title over key art with the trailer facade, the release window and the main action (wishlist / store page).
fields: Reveal trailer (video URL, poster still, duration)
sections.notes: The trailer is a facade: a still with a play button; the video and its network requests load only on press, and focus moves into the player. Key art can be generated from tokens (decorative, aria-hidden) when no artwork exists yet.

sections.purpose: Short press quotes and awards / festival laurels.
Three numbered pillars of the game (what you do, the feel, the hook), each with a still, alternating sides.
alternatives: feature-grid: more than three pillars, shorter text
fields: Per pillar: title, two sentences, screenshot with alt text

sections.purpose: Facts ledger: genre, platforms, players, length, languages, price window, release.
Screenshot filmstrip that opens in a lightbox.

fields: Entries: title, excerpt, date, reading time, author

sections.purpose: One launch email (or newsletter) and the store wishlist.
fields: What and when the email is sent
sections.notes: Newsletter variant of cta. Say clearly if it is only the launch email.

pages.purpose: All trailers and screenshots in one place.

sections.purpose: Every trailer as a click-to-load facade, newest one large.
fields: Per trailer: title, date, duration, poster still, video URL, captions file

alternatives: gallery: a plain grid without mosaic layout
fields: Screenshots with alt text and full-size files

pages.purpose: Everything a journalist or creator needs without emailing: facts, copy-ready texts, assets, team, review keys and embargo rules.

sections.purpose: What is here and the press contact.
Fact sheet plus copy-ready short and long descriptions and studio boilerplate, each with a copy button.
fields: Developer, publisher, release date, platforms, price, website

sections.purpose: Logos, key art, screenshots and texts, each downloadable on its own or ticked and bundled into one archive.
alternatives: export: when the bundle is generated on the server
fields: Per asset: name, format, size, file
sections.notes: Selection count and download result in a status region.

sections.purpose: Who made it and their roles.
How to request a review or streaming key.
alternatives: cta: a mailto action when there is no form
fields: Key request process and what to include

sections.purpose: Embargo, usage rights for footage and streaming / monetisation policy.
fields: Embargo and usage questions with answers

content: Game title, logo variants and key art
One-line pitch and short / long descriptions
Trailers (files or hosted URLs), posters, durations and captions
Facts: genre, platforms, modes, playtime, languages, age rating, release date
Store and wishlist links per platform
Press quotes and awards with sources
Studio boilerplate, team and press contact
Review key process, embargo date and footage usage policy

styles.name: dark heavy display
styles.why: Most games: dark, an extended heavy display face and one accent taken from the key art; the art and trailer do the talking.

styles.name: bright playful
styles.why: Cosy, family or puzzle games whose art is bright; rounder shapes and livelier motion match the tone.

pitfalls: Autoplaying or eagerly embedded trailers that load third-party players and cookies before the visitor presses play.
Trailers without captions, and screenshots with empty alt text.
Age rating, platforms or release date missing or out of date across pages.
A press kit that needs an email to get assets; journalists leave.
Store badges and platform logos used against the platform's brand rules.
Launch email signups without consent text or with a newsletter the visitor did not ask for.
Flashing effects in key art or trailers without a warning; respect reduced motion.
